items.title: CISA Adds Three Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
items.one_liner: CISA has added three actively exploited vulnerabilities to its KEV catalog, requiring immediate attention from federal agencies.
items.summary: CISA has updated its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog with three new entries confirmed to be under active exploitation. Under Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04, Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies are mandated to prioritize the remediation of these specific vulnerabilities on publicly exposed assets. CISA encourages all organizations to adopt this risk-based approach to vulnerability management to mitigate the threat posed by malicious actors.
key_facts: Action: Prioritize remediation of KEV catalog vulnerabilities
items.bottom_line: Federal agencies must prioritize patching these three newly identified vulnerabilities to comply with BOD 26-04.

items.title: CVE-2026-132165: Drupal Drupal Core Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
items.one_liner: A critical RCE in Drupal Core's installer requires immediate patching to prevent site takeover.
items.summary: Drupal Core contains a vulnerability in its installer that allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code or take over sites. By leveraging the install.php script under specific conditions, an attacker can attempt to reinstall the application. CISA has added this to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, requiring federal agencies to mitigate the issue by November 27, 2026.
items.bottom_line: If you manage Drupal instances, you must audit your installer exposure and apply vendor mitigations immediately to comply with CISA BOD 26-04.

items.title: CVE-2026-123633 Portfolio Status: Impact of NGINX Vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-123633, CVE-2026-123007) on Palo Alto Networks Products (Severity: CRITICAL)
items.one_liner: Critical NGINX vulnerabilities in Palo Alto Networks products allow RCE; disable HTTP/2 if patching is not immediate.
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks has identified two critical NGINX vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-123007) affecting its PAN-OS and Panorama products when HTTP/2 is enabled. The flaws involve use-after-free and integer underflow issues that can lead to worker process crashes or arbitrary code execution. The company has released remediations and advises customers to disable HTTP/2 if they cannot patch immediately.
items.bottom_line: Administrators must verify their PAN-OS/Panorama configurations and either patch or disable HTTP/2 to mitigate potential RCE attacks.

items.title: CVE-2026-132224: Optimizely Optimizely Web Experimentation External Control of Critical State Data Vulnerability
items.one_liner: A critical flaw in Optimizely allows attackers to inject malicious JavaScript into customer websites.
items.summary: Optimizely Web Experimentation contains a vulnerability in its account signup flow that allows attackers to impersonate users and modify Project JavaScript. This flaw enables the distribution of malicious, attacker-controlled JavaScript to browsers visiting customer websites. CISA has mandated federal remediation for this issue by November 27, 2026.
items.bottom_line: Organizations using Optimizely must treat this as a high-priority supply-chain risk and apply vendor patches immediately.

items.title: CVE-2026-131914: Idunno Idunno AntiCsrf Deserialization of Untrusted Data Vulnerability
items.one_liner: CISA warns of an unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability in Idunno AntiCsrf added to its KEV catalog.
items.summary: CISA has added a critical deserialization vulnerability in Idunno AntiCsrf to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. Tracked as CVE-2026-131914, the flaw allows unauthenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via object injection. The affected software products are potentially end-of-life or end-of-service, prompting CISA to advise federal agencies to immediately apply mitigations or discontinue use in compliance with BOD 26-04 directives.
key_facts: Vulnerability type: Deserialization of untrusted data / remote code execution via object injection
items.bottom_line: Federal agencies must immediately mitigate or remove Idunno AntiCsrf due to an actively managed remote code execution flaw tracked as CVE-2026-131914.

items.title: DOJ accuses former cyber executive of defrauding ransomware victims by secretly paying hackers
items.one_liner: A former ransomware recovery CTO was indicted by the DOJ for taking victim funds, secretly paying hackers, and pocketing the markup.
items.summary: The U.S. Department of Justice indicted Juan Ricardo Palacio Escobar, the 52-year-old former chief technology officer of RansomwareHelp, for allegedly defrauding cyberattack victims. Prosecutors state the firm claimed it could decrypt hacked files using proprietary technology with a 99% success rate, but instead secretly negotiated with and paid ransoms to hackers while pocketing the difference. Palacio Escobar allegedly used the fraudulent proceeds to purchase multiple properties in Florida and faces three counts of wire fraud carrying up to 20 years in prison each. This arrest follows a string of recent high-profile cases involving rogue cybersecurity professionals and ransomware gangs.
key_facts: Indicted individual: Juan Ricardo Palacio Escobar, 52
Charges: Three counts of wire fraud
items.bottom_line: Ransomware recovery firms that claim proprietary decryption without technical capability are running a fraud scheme by quietly paying extortionists.

items.title: From earlier – Maersk Confirms Data Breach As WhiteArmor Ransomware Demands $5 Million Maersk has confirmed a data breach after the WhiteArmor ransomware gang…
items.one_liner: Maersk confirms a data breach following WhiteArmor ransomware claims of a 100GB data theft and a $5M Bitcoin demand.
items.summary: Maersk has confirmed a data breach after the WhiteArmor ransomware gang claimed responsibility for stealing approximately 100GB of data from systems linked to LF Logistics, a company acquired by Maersk in 2022. The threat actors assert the stolen haul includes driver records, plaintext passwords, and dozens of administrative accounts, demanding a $5 million ransom in Bitcoin within 30 days. Maersk stated that current evidence indicates no sensitive data has been exposed and anticipates no disruption to operational activities.
items.bottom_line: Maersk faces a $5 million ransomware demand from the WhiteArmor gang following a data breach affecting a subsidiary's systems, though operations remain unaffected.

items.title: OpenAI and Cisco Unveil AI-Assisted Linux Security Tool to Block Exploits Before Patching
items.one_liner: A new eBPF-based runtime security tool that lets AI agents inject temporary, non-disruptive shields to block exploits before patches are ready.
items.summary: OpenAI and Cisco have launched Shirudo, an open-source Linux runtime security tool that uses AI agents to deploy eBPF-based shields. The tool allows defenders to block exploits in real-time without patching or system restarts by injecting targeted mitigations into the kernel. It is built on the foundation of the Tetragon security platform and is designed to protect infrastructure while security teams test and roll out permanent fixes.
items.bottom_line: You can now use AI-generated eBPF shields to protect vulnerable Linux systems from active exploits without requiring service downtime or immediate patching.

items.title: CrowdStrike agrees to buy Zscaler for $43.9 billion in network security expansion
items.one_liner: CrowdStrike is acquiring Zscaler for $43.9 billion to unite endpoint security and zero-trust network access for modern cloud architectures.
items.summary: CrowdStrike has agreed to acquire Zscaler in an all-stock transaction valued at approximately $43.9 billion to merge endpoint protection with cloud network security. The acquisition combines CrowdStrike's device and cloud workload monitoring with Zscaler's zero-trust network access control, addressing security requirements as corporate systems and AI agents connect directly to cloud applications. CrowdStrike plans to integrate device telemetry with network connection logs and cross-sell both platforms to Zscaler's roughly 8,000 customers. Zscaler CEO Jay Chaudhry will continue leading the business and join CrowdStrike's board upon closing, which is expected in the second half of fiscal 2028 pending regulatory and shareholder approvals.
key_facts: Expected close: Second half of CrowdStrike's 2028 fiscal year
items.bottom_line: The $43.9 billion acquisition of Zscaler by CrowdStrike merges endpoint intelligence and zero-trust networking under a single security platform.

items.title: Musk's plan to send a million SpaceX data satellites into space approved
items.one_liner: US regulators clear SpaceX to deploy a million low-Earth orbit satellites for orbital AI data centres.
items.summary: The US Federal Communications Commission has approved SpaceX's Starmind project, granting a licence to deploy up to one million satellites into low-Earth orbit to power space-based data centres for artificial intelligence. The solar-powered satellites will process AI workloads in orbit and relay data back to Earth via laser or Starlink links, with deployment required to begin by November 2033. The decision has drawn sharp criticism from rival firm Amazon and the American Astronomical Society, which warned that the massive constellation will severely disrupt astronomical observations and night sky visibility.
key_facts: Deployment phase milestones: 10% by November 2035, 50% by November 2038
items.bottom_line: SpaceX has secured FCC approval to launch a million low-Earth orbit satellites for orbital AI data centres, sparking fierce pushback from astronomers.

items.one_liner: Synology DiskStation Manager suffers from a critical CVSS 9.8 command injection vulnerability in its OAuth API allowing remote file access.
items.summary: A critical vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-120382 with a CVSS base score of 9.8, has been identified in the OAuth API of Synology DiskStation Manager (DSM). The flaw stems from improper neutralization of argument delimiters in a command, allowing remote unauthenticated attackers to read or write arbitrary files and execute denial-of-service attacks. The vulnerability affects multiple versions prior to patches 7.1.1-42962-10, 7.2.1-69057-14, 7.2.2-72806-11, 7.3.2-86009-6, and 7.4.1-90080-2.
items.bottom_line: Synology DSM administrators must immediately patch versions prior to 7.4.1-90080-2 and other fixed builds to mitigate a critical remote arbitrary file read/write vulnerability.

items.title: GitLab Patch Release and Security Update: 19.5.3, 19.4.5, 19.3.7, 19.2.10, 19.1.10, 19.0.11, 18.11.14
items.one_liner: GitLab security updates remove trust for compromised eMudhra intermediate CA certificates across multiple supported versions.
items.summary: GitLab has released patch versions 19.5.3, 19.4.5, 19.3.7, 19.2.10, 19.1.10, 19.0.11, and 18.11.14 for Community and Enterprise Editions to address CVE-2026-111943. The vulnerability involves compromised private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates, prompting GitLab to remove trust for them from its shipped certificate stores. Administrators running self-managed instances must upgrade GitLab, and also independently update self-hosted GitLab Runners to version 19.5.1 and GitLab AI Gateway components to corresponding patched versions.

items.title: 1Password breached through hijacked employee GitHub account, customer names and emails stolen
items.one_liner: 1Password experienced a backend breach via a compromised employee GitHub account, exposing user metadata and email records while vault contents remained safe.
items.summary: Password manager maker 1Password suffered a security breach after an attacker compromised a corporate employee's GitHub account on November 19, 2026. The intruder used the account to access private repositories, push malicious code to backend services, and download administrative user records containing names, email addresses, sign-in times, and public keys. Vault contents, master passwords, and secret keys remained completely secure and unaccessed. 1Password has revoked compromised tokens, rotated infrastructure secrets, lengthened account recovery codes from six to ten characters, and brought in cybersecurity experts to investigate.
items.bottom_line: An employee GitHub account compromise at 1Password resulted in the theft of customer administrative metadata, requiring users to remain vigilant against targeted phishing.

items.one_liner: Update the Palo Alto Networks GlobalProtect app on Windows to patch CVE-2026-0324, a local privilege escalation flaw in the OPSWAT SDK.
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks has disclosed an incorrect privilege management vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-0324, in the OPSWAT MetaDefender Endpoint Security SDK utilized by the GlobalProtect app on Windows devices. The flaw allows a locally authenticated non-administrative user to escalate their privileges to NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM without requiring special configurations. items.title: Two Italians killed in strike in Kuwait, as Iran denies responsibility
items.one_liner: Two Italian Rheinmetall defense technicians died in a drone strike on a facility in Kuwait, triggering mutual recriminations.
items.summary: Two Italian nationals working as technicians for German defense firm Rheinmetall were killed in a strike on a facility in Kuwait, with both Italy and Kuwait blaming Iran for the attack. The Kuwaiti defense ministry reported that four people were injured by falling shrapnel following the interception of incoming Iranian drones. Iran denied responsibility, with Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi describing the incident as suspicious and claiming it resembled a precooked recipe for war. The incident follows a series of regional exchanges of fire involving the United States, Israel, and Iran, heightening fears of a broader conflict.
items.bottom_line: Targeting of defense technicians in Gulf state facilities by suspected Iranian drones significantly escalates regional conflict risks.

items.title: Cisco Informational for Emergency Distrust of eMudhra Root and Intermediate Certificate Authorities
items.one_liner: A critical compromise of eMudhra intermediate certificates due to a key generation flaw requires immediate Cisco product remediation and trust store updates.
items.summary: A critical security compromise affecting eMudhra-managed Certificate Authorities was uncovered after a security researcher demonstrated that private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate certificates were fundamentally broken. The flaw stems from an unprecedented error during their Key Generation Ceremony in April 2025, allowing attackers to brute-force acquire these private keys within seconds. In response, Cisco has issued an advisory detailing impacted products across its portfolio—such as IOS XE, Secure Client, and Secure Email Gateways—and providing specific remediation steps. Administrators are advised to update trust stores and apply vendor patches immediately to mitigate potential exploitation of the compromised certificates.
items.bottom_line: Compromised eMudhra intermediate certificate private keys can be brute-forced instantly, necessitating immediate trust-store updates and vendor patches across enterprise networks.

items.title: Cisco UCS and UCS-Based Appliances UEFI Shell Secure Boot Bypass Vulnerability
items.one_liner: A UEFI Secure Boot bypass in Cisco UCS servers allows attackers to execute unauthorized code in the preboot environment.
items.summary: Cisco has disclosed a UEFI Secure Boot bypass vulnerability in its UCS servers and related appliances. An attacker with valid credentials or physical access can exploit the UEFI Shell to modify memory variables, effectively bypassing Secure Boot validation and executing unauthorized software. Cisco has released software updates to address this issue and advises users to apply them, as no workarounds exist. The vulnerability affects a wide range of UCS B-Series, C-Series, and various Cisco appliances.
key_facts: Affected: UCS B-Series, C-Series, X-Series, and various appliances
items.bottom_line: Apply Cisco's firmware updates immediately to prevent attackers from bypassing hardware-level security on your UCS infrastructure.

items.one_liner: Apache Solr versions 9.0.0 through pre-fix releases contain an 8.8 CVSS unauthenticated ping endpoint authorization bypass vulnerability.
items.summary: A high-severity vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-86312 with a CVSS score of 8.8 affects Apache Solr versions 9.0.0 through releases preceding fixed versions. The flaw allows low-privilege clients with health permissions to trigger unauthorized behavior via the ping endpoint due to unauthenticated default security.json templates. Users are advised to upgrade to versions 9.11.0 or 10.1.0 or restrict access to the /admin/ping endpoint in their authorization configurations. The default sample security configuration installed by the bin/solr CLI leaves this endpoint unauthenticated.

items.title: Agents didn’t break code review, they exposed it

items.summary: Software veteran John Crickett explains that the rise of coding agents has not broken code review, but rather exposed pre-existing flaws caused by delivery pressure and excessively large pull requests. Ultimately, teams cannot outsource accountability to AI tools and must ensure their verification practices evolve to match the volume of generated code.

items.title: Git security vulnerabilities announced
items.one_liner: Git 2.56.1 and backports fix six critical security flaws, including code execution during cloning and path traversal.
items.summary: The Git project has released security patches across multiple maintenance series, culminating in Git 2.56.1, to address six vulnerabilities including arbitrary code execution, path traversal, and stack corruption. CVE-2026-111760 involves an integer truncation vulnerability during index handling that permits an attacker-controlled Git server to overwrite repository metadata or execute code during cloning. Other fixed issues include path traversal via protocol v2 HEAD advertisements (CVE-2026-113408), stack corruption from excessive GPG signatures during merges (CVE-2026-114467), and out-of-bounds reads when applying compressed binary patches. Administrators and developers should update Git installations and dependent applications immediately.
key_facts: Affected versions: Git prior to 2.56.1 and backported series

items.one_liner: An unauthenticated RCE flaw in the Sneeit WordPress framework allows arbitrary function execution via direct AJAX callback handling.
items.summary: The Sneeit Framework plugin for WordPress versions up to and including 8.7 contains an unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability via the sneeit_compact_menu_mega_content AJAX action. items.title: Xen Security Advisory 535 v1 (CVE-2026-119781,CVE-2026-119782,CVE-2026-119783) - x86: Incorrect ordering of page-freeing and p2m flush
items.one_liner: Xen advisory XSA-535 addresses three x86 memory management flaws allowing guest privilege escalation and host DoS.
items.summary: Xen has released security advisory XSA-535 detailing three vulnerabilities tracked as CVE-2026-119781, CVE-2026-119782, and CVE-2026-119783 caused by incorrect ordering of page-freeing and p2m flushes on x86 architectures. This flaw enables privilege escalation, denial of service, and information leaks across Xen versions 4.7 and later. Downstream users are advised to update their stable branches and apply the corresponding official patches immediately.

items.title: I'll Have a Raw JSON, Please: Leaking a LangChain Assistant Through Format Coercion

items.summary: Researchers explore the security risks inherent in LLM-driven multi-agent software development systems, introducing two threat models: Malicious User with Benign Agents (MU-BA) and Benign User with Malicious Agents (BU-MA). items.title: AESP: A Human-Sovereign Economic Protocol for AI Agents with Privacy-Preserving Settlement
items.one_liner: AESP provides a cryptographic protocol ensuring AI agents execute high-speed financial transactions under strict human governance boundaries.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced the Agent Economic Sovereignty Protocol (AESP), a layered architecture that allows AI agents to transact autonomously on crypto-native infrastructure while remaining cryptographically bound to human-defined governance frameworks. items.title: SILK: Streaming Authentication with In-Place Checks for Low-bit LLM Inference
items.one_liner: SILK embeds keyed integrity checks directly into quantized low-bit LLM weights to prevent runtime tampering with minimal overhead.
items.summary: Researchers introduced SILK, a quantization-aware in-place integrity framework that protects low-bit large language model weights, activations, and KV caches against runtime tampering. items.title: PRECEPT: Security Self-Improvement of Coding Agents via Evolving Principles

items.summary: AI coding agents frequently reintroduce previously fixed security vulnerabilities in subsequent sessions despite successfully repairing them when shown failing tests. Principles are filtered to ensure functional code success while continuously hardening security across evolution steps. On unseen task families, agents equipped with PRECEPT significantly outperformed unaided baseline models in producing secure code.

items.title: The Detour Is the Danger: Preserving Security During LLM Agent Recovery
items.one_liner: ARGUS prevents workflow security downgrades in LLM agents by enforcing security obligations during autonomous failure recovery.
items.summary: LLM agents utilizing external tools and reusable skills often autonomously replan when operations fail, a process that can silently discard original security protections while preserving task functionality. Researchers identify this phenomenon as 'workflow security downgrade,' a failure-induced threat occurring without modifying prompt instructions or tool definitions. To mitigate this risk, they introduce ARGUS, an obligation-preserving framework combining resource-bound security evidence, isolated recovery plan validation, and execution-time enforcement. Evaluations across multiple models and task templates demonstrate that ARGUS prevents all observed protection-loss events during agent recovery.
items.bottom_line: Autonomous error recovery by LLM agents can silently strip away security constraints unless enforced by dedicated frameworks like ARGUS.

items.title: Agent Recovery Gone Wrong: Measuring Harm Beyond Duplicate Calls
items.one_liner: LLM agent error recovery frequently corrupts external states through duplicate actions and unintended deletions.
items.summary: Code-executing LLM agents frequently issue block writes that can fail midway, triggering autonomous recovery attempts where the agent rewrites and re-executes code. Researchers evaluating AppWorld agent trajectories found that 30 out of 143 confirmed partial executions resulted in harmful recoveries that persisted until the run ended. Two-thirds of these harmful recoveries duplicated operations, while the remainder deleted user data or executed incorrect writes, such as ordering the wrong product. Standard rule-based checkers searching for repeated calls catch 75% of duplications but miss 59% of total operational harm. The findings indicate that content-derived idempotency contracts are necessary to prevent state corruption during agent recovery.

items.bottom_line: Simple deduplication rules fail to catch the majority of state-corruption harms caused by autonomous agent error recovery, necessitating content-derived idempotency contracts.

items.title: CAPE: Coordinating Calibration and Search for Tool-Use Policies
items.one_liner: CAPE coordinates calibration and search to compile robust, optimal tool-use policies for LLM agents with 22% less compilation time.
items.summary: Tool-use policies often fail because receiving tools parse data under configurations unobservable to the LLM agent, necessitating continuous calibration and search. The authors present CAPE, a training-free compiler that maintains an executable policy at all times while dynamically directing calibration to calls that maximize improvement. By tightening bounds only where it enables early calibration termination, CAPE preserves completed configurations and certifies optimality. On CSV and JSON workflows, CAPE reached independent optima in 502 of 504 compilations while consuming 22.0% less compilation time than eager exact search.
key_facts: Success rate: 502 of 504 compilations reached the optimum
Time reduction: 22.0% less compilation time than eager exact search
Completion increase: 15.38 to 34.66 percentage points improvement over error-feedback revision
items.bottom_line: Jointly coordinating calibration and search allows LLM tool-use policies to compile faster while guaranteeing execution completeness.

items.title: AGL-SKILL: Coding Harnesses as Agentic Optimizers
items.one_liner: Coding agents can act as autonomous optimizers to iteratively improve task-specific workflows and skills without manual guidance.
items.summary: Researchers demonstrate that frontier language models operating as coding agents can function as effective agentic optimizers for skill development. Instead of relying on handcrafting or one-shot generation, the approach uses score-driven search and coding agents to iteratively tweak and refine task-specific skills, workflows, and prompts. Across five benchmarks, an unguided coding agent substantially improved target performance and outperformed existing published skill-optimization methods. This highlights the capability of autonomous agents to iteratively refine their own behavior when provided with clear performance metrics.
key_facts: Method: Coding agents as score-driven iterators
items.bottom_line: Autonomous coding agents can optimize their own task skills and workflows, outperforming existing skill-optimization methods.

items.title: Demystifying Real-world LLM Service Freeloading
items.one_liner: A measurement study of open-source projects reveals widespread LLM service freeloading by repackaging free web app inference into APIs.
items.summary: Researchers conducted a systematic measurement study of 513 open-source projects engaged in LLM service freeloading, tracing 1,588 inference paths across 64 upstream LLM services. They found that 93.0% of the repositories were created in 2026, with direct HTTP or WebSocket requests accounting for 83.2% of paths to reproduce product protocols. Additionally, 19.1% of paths utilized account selection or rotation to distribute requests across separate free allowances. An analysis of service terms revealed that 58 of 62 services explicitly prohibit practices such as automated access, account sharing, or service redistribution.
items.bottom_line: Over 90% of studied LLM service freeloading repositories repackage free AI inference into APIs, violating upstream provider terms.

items.summary: Drupal core is vulnerable to a critical remote code execution flaw, CVE-2026-132165 (Fail2Install), which allows unauthenticated attackers to trigger a site re-installation. items.one_liner: A WebKitGTK GLib DMA-BUF bounds-checking flaw enables out-of-bounds reads and potential sandbox escapes from a compromised WebProcess.
items.summary: A high-severity vulnerability, CVE-2026-135055 with a CVSS score of 8.0, resides in the GLib DMA-BUF path of WebKitGTK. The privileged UIProcess incorrectly trusted fds.size() as the plane count when processing AcceleratedBackingStore::DidCreateDMABufBuffer without verifying vector length matches. A compromised WebProcess can exploit this by sending mismatched vector lengths, triggering an out-of-bounds read in the UIProcess. This flaw can disclose memory, crash the process, and facilitate sandbox escapes.
items.bottom_line: WebKitGTK's failure to validate vector length matches in the GLib DMA-BUF path allows a compromised WebProcess to trigger an out-of-bounds read in the privileged UIProcess.

items.title: From Per-Frame Search to Practical Attacks: Investigating Adversarial Robustness of Multi-Agent Heterogeneous Cooperative Perception
items.one_liner: HetPoison achieves efficient adversarial feature attacks on heterogeneous cooperative perception systems without online gradients.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced HetPoison, a practical feature attack targeting multi-agent heterogeneous cooperative perception systems. Prior attacks relied on per-frame gradient descent requiring online detector queries and test-time labels, while heterogeneous architectures introduce barriers like blocking translation modules and sparse anchor gradients. HetPoison overcomes these obstacles by training a convolutional generator offline on a surrogate stack in a single forward pass, requiring no online gradients. Experiments on OPV2V-H demonstrate that HetPoison significantly reduces detection average precision while operating at up to 14,000 times lower online cost than baseline Adam-PGD methods.

Online cost reduction: Up to 14,000x lower online cost
items.bottom_line: HetPoison enables low-cost, offline-trained adversarial feature attacks that bypass architectural barriers in heterogeneous cooperative perception systems.

items.summary: Researchers investigated the tuning of numeric settings across multi-stage LLM pipelines applied to schema matching and mapping, revealing that joint optimization of accuracy and cost yields modest improvements. Because optimal settings vary even across individual columns within a single task, running dual configurations and deploying an LLM judge to resolve disagreements achieved a peak accuracy of 91.5% HR@1 at nearly six times the default cost.

items.title: Irreducible Governance Structure for Autonomous Agent Systems: Fair Allocation, Strategy-Proofness, and Multi-Scale Composition
items.one_liner: Multi-agent governance requires an irreducible multi-scale architecture because resource allocation imposes structural constraints that cannot be simplified.
items.summary: Autonomous agent governance in multi-agent systems requires managing resource allocation prior to execution. Allocation introduces unavoidable trade-offs between fairness, efficiency, and resistance to strategic manipulation, illustrated through impossibility results like Sybil amplification. Because these allocation constraints interact with execution atomicity, state enforcement, and behavioral drift, they cannot be resolved within a single control layer. The authors establish an irreducibility theorem proving that under finite observability, no multi-scale governance architecture can collapse these four dimensions without causing systematic failure modes.
items.bottom_line: Resource allocation in multi-agent systems acts as an irreducible first-class constraint that requires a multi-scale governance architecture.

claims.text: Allocation is not an auxiliary concern but a structural component of governance.
claims.support_span: In this paper, we show that allocation is not an auxiliary concern but a structural component of governance.

claims.text: No governance architecture can collapse these dimensions without loss of correctness or stability.

The benchmark uses an evidence-grounded multi-agent annotation framework to construct reliable ground-truth labels based on underlying facts and conversational contexts.
items.bottom_line: The InfoCon benchmark provides a robust testbed for evaluating multimodal LLMs on nuanced conversational information manipulation tactics like withholding and evasion.

items.title: Beyond the Efficiency-Efficacy Dilemma: A Critical Analysis of Transferability in Adversarial Malware Detection
items.one_liner: Single-step FGSM attacks demonstrated higher transferability against malware detection models than iterative PGD attacks.
items.summary: Researchers introduced the Adversarial AI Engine (AAIE), a platform for automated security stress-testing, to analyze transferability in adversarial malware detection using EMBER2018 against a Random Forest target. Counterintuitively, the single-step Fast Gradient Sign Method (FGSM) achieved a significantly higher attack success rate of 52.9% compared to the iterative Projected Gradient Descent (PGD) at 45.2%. The findings reveal that iterative attacks overfit surrogate networks and generate brittle perturbations, whereas FGSM yields more transferable adversarial examples. The study uses metrics like transferability score, evasion rate, and resilience index to evaluate model vulnerabilities under AI governance frameworks.

items.title: SecID: An LLM-Guided Framework for Threat-Aware Secondary Asset Identification with Quantitative RTL Analysis
items.one_liner: SecID is a new LLM-guided, multi-agent framework that combines RTL analysis and bounded dynamic evaluation to identify hidden hardware security assets.
items.summary: Researchers have proposed SecID, a multi-agent framework designed to identify threat-specific secondary security assets in pre-silicon hardware designs using deterministic register-transfer level (RTL) analysis, bounded dynamic evaluation, and LLM reasoning. While primary assets are obvious from design functionality, internal security-critical locations that facilitate complex data- and control-flow compromises are much harder to uncover without automated evaluation. Tested across seven open-source SoC and IP designs including openMSP430, NEORV32, and CV32E40P, SecID combines functional influence and attack mechanisms to provide a scalable path toward hardware security verification.
items.bottom_line: Automating pre-silicon security verification with frameworks like SecID enables hardware engineers to systematically uncover hidden secondary assets and complex data-flow vulnerabilities in SoC designs.

items.one_liner: GaokaoMathGen uses latent reasoning structures to generate high-difficulty Chinese mathematics examination problems with precise control.
items.summary: Researchers proposed GaokaoMathGen, a framework for generating Chinese Gaokao mathematics finale problems by utilizing latent reasoning structures instead of surface-level prompts. items.title: Modeling Event-Conditioned Emotional Expression Response with LLM Agents in a Synthetic Social Simulation
items.one_liner: A study on LLM agent emotional modeling shows they reproduce social patterns well but systematically underexpress anger, requiring calibration for behavioral simulation.

items.title: SpatialCraft: Evolving Procedural Intelligence from Experience and Skills for Spatial Reasoning Agents
items.one_liner: SpatialCraft is a self-evolving framework that lets frozen LLM agents optimize tool orchestration for spatial reasoning using experience and skills.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced SpatialCraft, a self-evolving framework designed to improve tool orchestration in frozen spatial reasoning agents without requiring parameter updates. items.title: Architecture-Agnostic Feature Synergy for Universal Defense Against Heterogeneous Generative Threats
items.one_liner: ATFS provides universal defense against heterogeneous generative threats by aligning high-level feature representations across architectures.
items.summary: Generative AI deployment faces security risks that are often exacerbated by architecture-specific defense mechanisms, creating fragile silos against heterogeneous generative threats. items.title: Sketching for First Order Method: Efficient Algorithm for Low-Bandwidth Channel and Vulnerability
items.one_liner: Random sketching in federated learning reduces communication costs but risks data leakage, which can be mitigated with differential privacy noise.
items.summary: Sketching randomly compresses high-dimensional data into lower dimensions to reduce computational overhead in large-scale machine learning, but applying random sketching alone to federated learning gradients fails to provide formal data privacy. Researchers propose a distributed learning sketching scheme that reduces per-round communication costs while guaranteeing convergence, and present a gradient-matching attack proving that an attacker tracking a client over multiple rounds can recover local data. As a countermeasure, the authors demonstrate that adding Gaussian noise to the sketched gradients achieves differential privacy while preserving model convergence rates for convex objectives, bounded by an additive error dependent on the privacy level and sketch dimension.
items.bottom_line: Distributed learning algorithms using sketching require added Gaussian noise to prevent gradient-matching data reconstruction attacks while maintaining communication efficiency.

items.title: Are You Still the Agent I Authorized? Earned Authority under a Fixed Ceiling for Evolving Agents
items.one_liner: Researchers propose an authorization continuity framework to securely bound the evolving capabilities of long-lived AI agents under fixed ceilings.
items.summary: Long-lived AI agents evolve post-deployment by acquiring skills and mutating workflows, creating authorization challenges where live grants may no longer align with user intent. items.title: Look Before You Commit: Visual-Evidence-Guided Decoding for Multimodal Diffusion Language Models
items.one_liner: CD-APC is a training-free decoding method that prevents hallucinations in multimodal diffusion models by validating token commits against visual evidence.
items.summary: Multimodal diffusion language models rely on confidence scores to determine when to commit tokens during generation, but confidence cannot distinguish whether a candidate comes from image evidence or the language prior. Across two backbones and five benchmarks, CD-APC consistently improves performance by ensuring outputs are grounded in stable visual evidence.

items.bottom_line: Multimodal diffusion model hallucinations can be suppressed by replacing confidence scores with contrastive visual-evidence-guided decoding.

items.title: RegionAlign: Manipulating Parameter Layouts for Localized Fault Injection on LLMs and VLMs

items.title: C3H: Compression-to-Consensus Criteria Hijacking in Multimodal LLM Recommender Systems
items.one_liner: C3H demonstrates an inference-time attack exploiting compression-to-consensus biases in multimodal LLM recommender systems.
items.summary: Multimodal large language model recommender systems often rely on multimodal compression and cross-modal fusion to suppress anomalies, but these mechanisms can expose a compression-to-consensus (C2C) bias in ranking decisions. Signals that remain salient after compression and receive consistent cross-modal support gain disproportionate influence, creating an exploitable vector for content manipulation. The authors introduce C3H, an inference-time attack that tailors a target item's multimodal content to align with these implicit decision criteria, substantially increasing target exposure while preserving overall recommendation utility.
items.bottom_line: Multimodal LLM recommenders are vulnerable to inference-time content manipulation attacks that exploit cross-modal consensus biases.

items.title: Evaluating Frontier-Model Agent Skills with Open-Weight Models in a Science Gateway

items.summary: Researchers evaluated how open-weight models perform when replacing frontier models to power specialist coding agents within the PegasusAI Studio science gateway. The evaluation also exposed operational challenges where evaluation failures can be misconstrued as model failures when access restrictions are improperly enforced.

items.title: Multi-agent System for Automatic Discovery of Pareto-optimal Meta-solvers for PDEs
items.one_liner: An evolutionary multi-agent LLM framework running locally on laptops successfully discovers Pareto-optimal solvers for complex PDEs.
items.summary: Researchers introduce a multi-agent framework where language-model agents propose, critique, implement, and evaluate solver configurations for discretized partial differential equations. Tested on small open-weight language models on a single laptop against single-agent baselines across four problems, the system delivers 47 and 48 convergent hybrid solvers out of 60 candidates for three-dimensional acoustic scattering and elasticity. For coupled dynamic thermoelasticity, it completes 98 of 100 transient candidates and reaches accuracy 15 times faster in 2D and achieves a 20 times lower displacement error in 3D compared to a single agent.

items.title: TableRouter: Query-Aware Evidence Construction for Long-Table Question Answering
items.one_liner: TableRouter improves long-table reasoning in LLMs by routing between computed statistics and targeted row retrieval.
items.summary: Researchers introduce TableRouter, a training-free framework designed to handle long-table question answering by dynamically routing queries between a computation route for full-table question-conditioned statistics and a coverage route for retrieving relevant rows and column summaries. Furthermore, on long tables from previously unseen databases, TableRouter achieves 35.8% accuracy using Qwen2.5-7B compared to 16.4% for the strongest external baseline. A controlled experiment shows that providing explicitly computed statistics raises accuracy by up to 40.0 points.

items.title: GreenDynaMix: Thermal-Aware Dynamic Mixed-Precision MoE LLM Inference Systems
items.one_liner: GreenDynaMix combines DVFS thermal management and MoE-router precision tuning to reduce GPU aging during LLM inference.
items.summary: Sustained inference in large language models generates severe heat that accelerates silicon aging and lowers GPU reliability, forcing real-time frequency scaling that degrades throughput or accuracy. To resolve this, researchers propose GreenDynaMix, a runtime system that couples a DVFS-based thermal manager with a dynamic precision-tuning throughput compensator. The system uses a sensitivity-aware allocator driven by Mixture-of-Experts router signals to assign higher precision to critical experts while lowering it elsewhere. Experiments across server, desktop, and embedded platforms show that GreenDynaMix cuts the temperature-induced aging rate of GPUs during LLM inference by 25% to 33%. Without offline profiling or retraining, it recovers throughput at a perplexity cost of 0.9% to 1.6% using 8-bit/4-bit mixed precision, and up to 9.4% when constrained to 4-bit/2-bit precision.

items.bottom_line: Thermal-aware dynamic mixed-precision systems can reduce GPU aging during LLM inference by up to 33% without requiring model retraining.

items.title: TACT-Bench: Testing Adaptive Conversational Threats against Tool-Use Agents
items.one_liner: TACT-Bench evaluates policy-governed tool-use AI agents against stateful, adaptive conversational manipulation attacks.
items.summary: Researchers introduced TACT-Bench, a new stateful benchmark designed to test adaptive conversational threats against policy-governed tool-use agents. items.bottom_line: Current defense methods fail to adequately protect tool-use AI agents against adaptive conversational manipulation and policy escalation.

items.title: Agent Evaluation Without Ground Truth: A Null Proportion Perspective
items.one_liner: A new statistical framework uses e-values to evaluate autonomous agent trajectories without relying on explicit ground truth.
items.summary: As autonomous coding and science agents gain end-to-end execution capabilities, evaluating their performance against binary ground-truth labels becomes increasingly insufficient due to noisy trajectories and dynamic experimental outcomes. items.title: PRETZEL: A Benchmark for Cyclic Peptide Structure Prediction

items.title: Contrastive On-Policy Self-Distillation for LLM Unlearning
items.one_liner: Contrastive On-Policy Self-Distillation improves LLM unlearning by tracking and distilling policy trajectories against knowledge-reduced targets.
items.summary: Large language model unlearning techniques frequently rely on fixed forget sequences that offer negative supervision without tracking the actual states visited by the evolving unlearned policy. items.title: icsScanner: Safe Active Vulnerability Scanning for ICS and OT Networks
items.one_liner: icsScanner is an active vulnerability scanner designed specifically for ICS and OT networks with strict pre-probe fingerprinting and safety gates.
items.summary: Industrial control systems (ICS) and operational technology (OT) environments present unique scanning risks where active probes can crash fragile twenty-year-old programmable logic controllers (PLCs). To address this domain gap, security researchers developed icsScanner, an active vulnerability scanner built specifically for OT networks. The tool implements safety guardrails by fingerprinting targets before every probe, enforcing global and per-target rate limiting, and capping confidence levels based strictly on evidentiary support. It covers 250 checks across 29 protocol families, including Modbus, S7comm, OPC UA, PROFINET, and DNP3, while maintaining strict architectural separation to prevent physical safety risks.

items.summary: France's political mainstream faces a potential wipe-out in the upcoming April-May 2027 presidential elections as hard-right and hard-left leaders Marine Le Pen and Jean-Luc Mélenchon dominate poll ratings. While figures like European Parliament MP Raphaël Glucksmann represent the soft-left, allies are increasingly gravitating toward Mélenchon's coalition. items.summary: On November 10, 2026, the React team published CVE-2026-126187 through GitHub's CNA. The bug is unauthenticated remote code execution in React Server Components (RSC). Three bundler packages implementing the RSC Flight transport are affected: react-server-dom-webpack, react-server-dom-parcel, and react-server-dom-turbopack. Fixes shipped the same day across four release lines. The advisory names one precondition: responses must "transport multiple typed arrays and an attacker-controlled value." items.title: Argentina bars Central Bank from printing money to fund government spending
items.one_liner: Argentina's legislature passed a bill barring the Central Bank from printing money for government expenses, backed by President Javier Milei.
items.summary: Argentina’s Chamber of Deputies has given final approval to a landmark bill prohibiting the country's Central Bank from printing money to finance government spending. Pushed forward by libertarian President Javier Milei, the law defines the bank's primary mission as maintaining currency value, effectively ending nearly two decades of monetary financing that previously drove inflation past 200 percent. Meanwhile, the Senate advanced separate legislation to suspend the country's primary elections ahead of the upcoming presidential vote, drawing fierce criticism from political opponents who accuse the administration of altering democratic rules to secure reelection.

items.title: First Attack, Final Offensive: The Dark Forest on an Open Roster
items.one_liner: Game-theoretic models of tactical preemption show that open player rosters break deterministic survival strategies unless specific probability thresholds on unobserved agents hold.
items.summary: This study analyzes the Dark Forest decision problem in game theory when the player roster is open and agents lack complete lists of nearby participants. The authors demonstrate that when the roster is open, the survival-maximizing strategy holds true regardless of beliefs if and only if agents assign a specific low threshold probability to unobserved agent intervention. Without strict assumptions, this threshold falls below one-half because unobserved third parties may react differently to alternate courses of action. Consequently, rational choices cannot be guaranteed without making explicit assumptions about unobserved actors in the environment.
items.bottom_line: Unobserved agents in open-roster environments invalidate universal preemption arguments unless strict probabilistic assumptions are met.

items.title: Conservative Overlap Fuzzy Rough Sets for Incomplete Data
items.one_liner: The Conservative Overlap Fuzzy Rough Set model reduces attribute dimensionality in incomplete datasets, delivering smaller reducts without improving classifier accuracy.
items.summary: Attribute reduction in incomplete information systems is complicated by missing values that disrupt traditional rough set equivalence classes. To solve this, researchers introduce the Conservative Overlap Fuzzy Rough Set (COFRS) model, which applies a global penalty to missing values via a weighted overlap metric divided by total attributes. Evaluated across 11 UCI benchmarks with missing rates spanning 0.15% to 20.46%, COFRS successfully produced the smallest attribute reducts on average, averaging 4.1 attributes compared to 5.0-11.2 for alternative methods. However, the gains are limited to data compactness rather than predictive accuracy, as kNN and RBF-SVM classifiers showed no significant accuracy improvements.
key_facts: Average reduct size: 4.1 attributes for COFRS versus 5.0-11.2 for alternatives
items.bottom_line: COFRS achieves smaller attribute reduct sizes for incomplete data by globally penalizing missing values rather than matching them as wildcards.

items.title: Russian Legal AI Reasoning Benchmark: AI Judge Swap Flips Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.2 Astra Order
items.one_liner: A Russian legal reasoning benchmark reveals that AI model leaderboards shift significantly depending on which LLM serves as the judge.
items.summary: The second Lexometrica Ground Truth evaluation run on Russian Supreme Court cases demonstrates that AI model rankings are highly sensitive to the choice of the grading judge. When Claude Opus 5.5 grades the 15-model benchmark, it finishes 0.053 points ahead of GPT-6.2 Astra, but when xAI's Grok 4.7 judges instead, Claude falls 0.010 points behind Astra. Tested across 30 legal cases using the IRAC legal analysis framework without search tools, top models like Claude Fable 5.2 and Gemini 4 Carbon cluster tightly within a narrow 0.09 band. Developer Nikita Polyakov notes that the closed dataset and overlapping confidence intervals mean models can be reliably separated into only five or six distinct quality tiers.
key_facts: Dataset size: 30 Russian Supreme Court cases
Evaluation methodology: IRAC scheme (Issue, Rule, Application, Conclusion)
items.bottom_line: AI legal reasoning benchmarks are vulnerable to judge bias, where swapping the grading model can flip top-tier rankings between competing vendors.

items.title: ICE Maintains Flagship Gilt Futures Design After Market Feedback
items.one_liner: ICE's decision to preserve the existing gilt futures design removes uncertainty for UK government bond market positioning.
items.summary: Intercontinental Exchange Inc. has decided to maintain the design of its flagship gilt futures contract for UK government bonds after gathering feedback from market participants. The exchange dropped a proposal that would have restricted contract settlement eligibility to gilts with an original term to maturity of 16 years or less, which aimed to address valuation distortions caused by aged bonds. Analysts noted that the informal consultation had already cheapened aged bonds relative to eligible gilts, a dynamic that is expected to reverse once normal trading resumes. The decision avoids changes to contracts tracking bonds with a maturity of around 10 years.
key_facts: Rejected proposal maturity: 16 years or less

items.title: Novinarya: An Android stealer that hides its live C2 in a shop bio
items.summary: Scan this sample for a command server and you find nothing: no URL, no IP, nothing to block. Behind a fake “Smart System Security” app, this Iranian banking and crypto stealer keeps its server out of the binary and reads it at run time from the bio of a seller’s profile on a legitimate marketplace, rotating it with a single edit no new sample needed. Four earlier builds resolved to a profile the marketplace had already banned, a dead end. This one was still live, so for once the trail runs the whole way, from an encrypted byte in the manifest to the running C2 at (theapi.the-x-services[.]xyz). items.title: Monitoring the Paper Machine: AI Research in the Age of Acceleration
items.summary: Abstract Coding agents such as Codex and Claude Code are increasingly used as research agents. As authors, reviewers, and area chairs delegate more of their work to AI, conferences—and more generally the research field—gradually become an “AI system” in its own right. We call this evolving system, from individual conferences to the field as a whole, the “Paper Machine”. AI may accelerate its output beyond human capacity to understand or check it, while the incentives shaping that output may favour proxies for progress over progress itself. Monitoring this Paper Machine therefore requires tracking not only how much research is produced, but also how it is produced, presented, and evaluated.

It did well, partly because at that time APIs had become hugely popular in the development world while most cybersecurity content still assumed you were poking at a server-rendered web app. The shift from server rendered to client-side + API is well and truly done now. In 2026 the API is the application for most of what you’ll test. The browser, the mobile app, the smart TV, the partner integration, the AI agent calling a tool, they’re all just clients talking to the same handful of endpoints behind the scenes.
